response.summary: The patch introduces two new files that contain Python code but are named with a ".txt" extension. The code itself is trivial: a "refresh" function that always returns True and a test that merely asserts True. No real functionality is implemented, no imports or error handling are present, and the tests do not validate any behavior. This suggests placeholder or incomplete work.
flag_reasons: File extensions do not match content (Python code in .txt files)
Functions are trivial and not used anywhere
Tests are placeholders and do not verify functionality
Potential naming conflicts with existing modules

findings.comment: File contains Python code but has a .txt extension; consider renaming to .py.
The "refresh" function always returns True; no error handling or token logic implemented.
Test file has a .txt extension; should be .py.
Test merely asserts True; does not exercise the "refresh" function.
